Hi everyone,

I am struggling with the process of sliding and resampling my semilandmarks.

First of all, I don't understand the difference between sliding and resampling.

Here is a sample of my coordinate matrix: I want to resample the curve  which lies between my fixed landmarks 1 and 2. I would like to resample the semilandmarks with a density of n=100.

Best regards,

Bruno

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Resamplig curves
parts:
Bruno,

 

The sliding of semilandmarks means that during the GPA superimposition, their locations move along the curve or surface such that the bending energy or Procrustes distance between that specimen and the reference is minimized. For curve points, they slide between other points that the user specifies (e.g., landmark 3 slides between 2 & 4).

 

Resampling is a general statistical process of obtaining values from a set of values. In the case of resampling points along a curve, the curve is specified, and one chooses how many semilandmarks points along it are used to represent that curve. This is a pre-processing step that occurs before GPA. If one is reading shape files digitized from StereoMorph, the ‘readland.shapes’ function allows you to specify how many points are used for each curve.

 

Finally, I had a quick look at your csv file. I do not know how that was generated but it contains quite a few landmarks with identical coordinates. Those should not be used, as they are redundant.


Dean

messages.author: baf6eb7bae06984d
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Resamplig curves
parts:
If you have the 3D model in a standard format (e.g, obj/ply), you can give  curve resampling in 3D Slicer a try. See https://github.com/SlicerMorph/Tutorials/tree/main/Markups_2
This can give you some idea about whether you have issues with your model.

I don't know how Stratovan does it, but in 3D Slicer if you have missing vertices along the path of the curve, and you force the points to be constrained by the model's surface, and finally you are sampling very densely, some semiLMs may get pushed to the same vertex (since that's the closest one they can be projected on) and hence end up having same coordinate.
